rdf:Description.dc:title: Grounds of the Department of Agriculture
rdf:Description.dc:description: Even before President Abraham Lincoln officially created a Department of Agriculture in 1862, the Bureau of Agriculture, part of the Patent Office, was growing crops on the National Mall, conducting research, and distributing seeds across the country. In 1865, the Department of Agriculture expanded its presence on the Mall, creating landscaped gardens and growing experimental crops. By the 1930s, formal gardens surrounded its main building, as shown in this photograph.
